baseline_models.focus_anchor: The rhetorical demand for aid, the deliberate taking of a qurban as gods other than God, and the helpers' disappearance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Agents acquire objects of worship as means of approach and thereby load the relation with an expectation of aid. When the supposed helpers cannot be found at the test, their absence exposes both the mediating arrangement and its claimed efficacy as fabricated.

activation_trace.role: Aid and making one prevail supply the performance expected from the adopted mediators and tested by the opening question.
Making or acquiring something for oneself marks the gods as deliberately installed relational assets rather than accidental errors.
Otherness and lower rank locate the acquired gods outside and beneath the divine endpoint they were meant to mediate.
Being made an object of worship identifies both the true divine pole and the manufactured divine substitutes in the relation.
An offering or means used to seek approach supplies the mediating function for which the adopted gods were valued.
Loss and inability to locate a thing turn failed help into the concrete nonavailability of the alleged helpers.
A lie diverted from truth names the false claim that this installed relation could secure approach and aid.
Inventing falsehood makes the failed mediation an authored construction repeatedly maintained by its adherents.

changed_reading.before: A general rebuke that false gods did not help their worshippers.
changed_reading.after: A failed nearness contract: worshippers deliberately installed mediating gods to secure approach and expected aid, but nonappearance under test discloses the whole relation as their own fabrication.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The qurban-as-gods construction beside the demand that those adopted figures render aid.
baseline_models.mechanism: The nearness term can evoke a ruler's intimates and courtiers as well as an offering. On this reading the adopted gods are imagined as insiders close enough to convey access and patronage; their disappearance strips them of the courtly presence on which that claim depends.

activation_trace.role: Favored intimates and a ruler's inner circle supply the social model of divine access assigned to the adopted gods.
Nearness that remains short of the goal positions the alleged courtiers as intermediate rather than ultimate.
Deliberate acquisition makes patron status something the worshippers confer and maintain.
Support and prevailing define the patronage service expected from figures claimed to be near the sovereign.
Vanishing from view removes the supposed insiders precisely when their presence should matter.

changed_reading.before: Qurban names only sacrificial offerings made to separate gods.
changed_reading.after: The construction can also stage those gods as self-appointed divine courtiers: claimed insiders expected to patronize their clients, yet absent when their access is tested.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence of taking, seeking nearness, going astray or missing, inversion, and fabrication.
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing pair need not be redundant labels for lying. Inversion supplies a directional operation that turns attachment from its proper end, while fabrication supplies the making of the mediating device; the vanished gods reveal a constructed system of diversion.

activation_trace.role: Making something one's own begins the human construction of the substitute relation.
A means intended to bring one near supplies the advertised direction of the constructed device.
Deviation from the intended course registers the device's actual directional result.
Turning a thing away from its proper face supplies the reversal by which alleged approach becomes diversion.
Cutting and joining material to fashion something supplies a controlled making analogy for the manufactured religious system.

changed_reading.before: The final two expressions simply repeat that the worshippers lied.
changed_reading.after: The ending exposes a made diversion: they fashioned a means advertised as approach, but its operation reversed direction and left both adherents and helpers lost.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier sequence turns the focus question into a diagnosis of a nonreciprocal relationship. The worshippers call, receive no answer, and address beings unaware of the call; at gathering, the same beings become enemies and repudiate the worship. Failure to help is therefore not one missed intervention but the exposure and reversal of an empty channel.

activation_trace.role: Expected aid is the focus-side service whose relational preconditions the earlier sequence tests.
Seeking approach supplies the intended bond that the call-and-answer sequence shows to be nonreciprocal.
Calling and drawing another by speech establishes the attempted communication channel to the other-than-God addressees.
Returning speech or answering supplies the reciprocal act explicitly absent from that channel.
Inattention that leaves something outside awareness explains why the call never becomes a mutual relation.
Enmity turns passive nonresponse into an active reversal of the patron-client expectation.
Submissive worship names the human investment that receives neither recognition nor aid and is finally repudiated.

structural_cues: 46:4-6 moves from inspecting invoked beings, through nonresponse and unawareness, to gathered hostility and repudiation.
The repeated worshipper-addressee relation is the same relation whose capacity for aid is tested in 46:28.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies invocation, absent answer, unawareness, worship, and eventual enmity; I infer that usable aid presupposes recognition and reciprocity, so the sequence diagnoses the channel itself as empty. A live alternative is that 46:6 marks only a future reversal rather than present relational nullity.

changed_reading.before: The adopted gods happen to fail during one crisis.
changed_reading.after: Their failed aid reveals a channel that was never reciprocal: call meets no answer or awareness, and the supposed bond ultimately reverses into enmity and repudiation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the earlier context, fabrication and inversion are accusations directed at the message, while the warning is charged with turning people away from their gods. The focus demonstrative returns those same operations to the worshippers: the allegedly diverting message is not the fabrication; their divinized mediation is the manufactured diversion.

activation_trace.role: Directional inversion in the focus supplies the operation whose ownership is reassigned by the contextual accusations.
Invented falsehood in the focus identifies the worshippers' system as the actual object of the repeated fabrication charge.
The repeated accusation of invented falsehood supplies the contested label that the focus later redirects.
Calling the received message an old lie establishes the worshippers' prior assignment of the falsehood label.
The charge of being turned away supplies the precise directional accusation reversed by the focus.
The worshipped gods identify what the speakers fear losing when they portray warning as diversion.

structural_cues: 46:8, 46:11, and 46:22 repeatedly place fabrication or diversion language inside contested speech before 46:28's demonstrative judgment.
The immediate destruction narrative intervenes before the focus returns the charge to the failed divine substitutes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated accusation vocabulary and a later demonstrative judgment; I infer a deliberate polemical return of the labels from revelation to the manufactured cult. The recurrence could instead be non-directional thematic repetition, leaving the focus as a simple independent verdict.

changed_reading.before: The ending independently labels idolatry as lie and fabrication.
changed_reading.after: The ending adjudicates a struggle over labels: those who called revelation fabricated and diverting are shown to have fabricated the very diversion they defended.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding cloud scene activates the rain-and-relief branch of aid. A cloud is read as incoming rain, but the adversative reversal identifies a punitive wind; it destroys, endowed faculties do not suffice, and signs are turned through different presentations. The focus question then repeats that perceptual failure socially: a form expected to deliver relief proves to be an inverted carrier of ruin, just as adopted patrons expected to help disappear.

activation_trace.role: Rain as rescue and life-giving aid opens the focus verb to the material expectation staged by the approaching cloud.
Winds that shift from their expected courses provide a weather-shaped image for the focus's inversion.
Water descending from cloud supplies the community's expected rescue reading of the visible form.
Rain associated with punishment keeps the same material sign while reversing its expected benefit.
Blowing wind supplies the actual carrier concealed beneath the mistaken rain-cloud interpretation.
Painful punishment supplies the destructive payload that replaces expected relief.
Extirpating destruction makes the consequence of the mistaken rescue reading materially complete.
Sufficiency and availing establish the negative utility test that immediately anticipates the focus's failed help.
Turning something through different states supplies the final transition from varied signs to the focus's exposed inversion.

structural_cues: 46:24 explicitly reverses the inhabitants' rain interpretation before 46:25-27 narrates destruction, non-availing capacities, and varied signs.
46:28 follows without a scene break and asks why the adopted divine means did not provide aid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a cloud called rain, an explicit reversal to punitive wind, destruction, non-availing faculties, and the focus root's rain-rescue branch; I infer that adjacency carries this material rescue failure into the patronage question. The live alternative is that the focus verb retains only ordinary social or military help with no weather echo.

changed_reading.before: The false gods simply fail to intervene after a destroyed people call on them.
changed_reading.after: Their failure repeats the cloud's inverted promise: what was read as a vehicle of rescue carried ruin, so apparent nearness and apparent relief are exposed by the same misrecognition.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the focus, a group is turned toward the recitation, hears with understanding, comes into presence, listens silently, and then urges its people to answer God's caller. Answering yields protective adjacency, while refusal leaves no escape and no supporting patrons besides Him. This supplies a counter-model of approach: nearness is enacted by receptive response, not manufactured by acquiring divine intermediaries.

activation_trace.role: Claimed intimate access supplies the false patronage model that the following responsive sequence replaces.
Aid is the failed outcome against which genuine answering and protection are measured.
Being turned toward a new face begins a successful redirection rather than the focus's deceptive diversion.
Hearing as understanding and compliance makes reception functionally responsive rather than merely acoustic.
Presence, witnessing, and nearness supply an enacted approach that contrasts with claimed cultic proximity.
Attentive silence supplies the receptive posture through which the new relation becomes effective.
Returning the call supplies the reciprocal act missing from the false-god relationship.
The voiced summons identifies the legitimate call whose answer establishes relation.
Neighboring protection supplies the real shelter promised through response, countering merely alleged patronage.
Failure to outrun or escape closes the possibility that another route can compensate for refusing the call.
Otherness marks the same alternative divine space occupied by the failed intermediaries in the focus.
Loving alliance and support name the patronage explicitly unavailable outside the legitimate relation.
Deviation from the right course names the condition produced by refusing the responsive path.

structural_cues: 46:29-31 forms a response chain: redirection, hearing, presence, attentive silence, return to a people, and an appeal to answer.
46:32 closes the chain with no escape and no patrons other than God, directly echoing the focus's other-than-God helpers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the response chain, protective adjacency, and explicit denial of other patrons; I infer that it is a positive counter-model to the focus's purchased nearness. A live alternative is that the post-focus episode illustrates warning and accountability without defining the earlier qurban relation.

changed_reading.before: The ayah only negates access through false intermediaries.
changed_reading.after: The following sequence also discloses an alternative approach: turn, attend, understand, and answer the legitimate call; protective nearness follows response, while manufactured patrons provide neither answer nor aid.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates peripheral water-channel, reservoir, water-seeking, and rain-deprivation branches across several focus roots. It remains anchored in the focus's aid, taking, approach, and inversion lexemes and is materially activated by the adjacent cloud scene. Downstream prose should present it only as a hydrological analogy for failed mediation, never as the direct lexical translation of the ayah.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The cluster of aid, deliberate taking, qurban-nearness, and inversion immediately after a cloud expected to bring rain.

activation_trace.role: Watercourses arriving from afar into a collection point supply a channel model for expected aid.
A hollow that captures and retains water supplies the receiving infrastructure assigned to the adopted means.
Moving toward a water source supplies the promised motion from need toward relief.
Land deprived of rain supplies the failed endpoint of a channel that promised water but delivered none.
Rainwater from the cloud provides the adjacent material expectation that activates the focus cluster.
Wind replacing expected rain supplies the misrouting event that defeats the imagined delivery system.

changed_reading.before: The false gods fail only as personal helpers.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the cult resembles a misrouted water-delivery system: channels, capture, and approach promise relief, but the arriving wind leaves the expected recipients without rain or aid.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's non-dominant mapped inventory for the final focus root, activating slackening after intensity rather than the ordinary fabrication sense. It remains valid as a secondary echo anchored in that exact focus occurrence and the failed-help sequence. Downstream prose must qualify it as an associative activation and must not replace the ordinary meaning of fabrication with faltering.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The final focus verb's split root mapping, following the helpers' failure and disappearance.

activation_trace.role: Weakening and subsiding after sharpness supply an echo in which the alleged patrons' manufactured potency slackens at the decisive test.
The demand for effective aid provides the test against which that exploratory slackening becomes visible.
Disappearance supplies the observable collapse that permits the faltering echo without changing the base lexical reading.
The prior failure of endowed capacities to avail supplies a nearby pattern of apparent power becoming functionally inert.

changed_reading.before: The closing verb only states that the worshippers kept inventing claims.
changed_reading.after: Without displacing that meaning, the split inventory permits an exploratory echo: the potency they fabricated for their patrons slackens into inactivity exactly when aid is demanded.

strongest_changes: The nonresponse sequence changes one failed rescue into exposure of a relation that never possessed recognition or reciprocity and ultimately reverses into enmity.
The adjacent cloud scene activates aid as rain-relief, making the focus repeat a concrete reversal in which an apparent vehicle of rescue carries destruction.
The post-focus answer chain supplies a positive counter-model: receptive hearing and response create protective nearness, while acquired patrons offer neither answer nor aid.
Repeated accusations of fabrication and diversion are returned to the worshippers, so the ending resolves a contested attribution rather than merely adding generic blame.
summary.what_was_special: The focus supports several coexisting mechanisms: ritual mediation, courtier-style patronage, a constructed directional diversion, a rain-rescue reversal, and a contrast between purchased proximity and responsive proximity. Peripheral hydrological branches and the non-dominant split mapping preserve activations that a conservative synthesis would likely erase.
remaining_uncertainties: The qurban construction can sustain offering, means-of-approach, and courtier-intimacy readings without forcing one syntactic resolution.
The rain-rescue model depends on immediate context activating a peripheral aid branch; ordinary social help remains fully live.
The post-focus response chain may be a deliberate counter-model of nearness or a separate illustration of warning and accountability.
The faltering sense from the non-dominant final-root mapping is associative and should never displace the primary fabrication reading.
